### GO-2026-6452 — Panic via negative shared-string index in github.com/xuri/excelize
- Aliases: CVE-2026-59162, GHSA-fx5j-qcqg-grpf | Published: 2026-09-16 | Modified: 2026-09-24 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/github.com/xuri/excelize/v2: introduced:0 fixed:2.11.0

In github.com/xuri/excelize/v2, parsing a spreadsheet cell with a negative shared-string index causes a runtime panic. The shared-string lookup in xlsxC.getValueFrom checks only the upper bound of the parsed index against the shared-string slice length, causing negative indices (such as -1) to bypass validation and trigger an out-of-bounds slice access when reading cells via APIs such as GetCellValue or GetRows.

References:
- https://github.com/qax-os/excelize/security/advisories/GHSA-fx5j-qcqg-grpf [ADVISORY]
- https://github.com/qax-os/excelize/commit/93f0b3caed37f21ef5079e3259c6c21dcfe68453 [FIX]
- https://github.com/qax-os/excelize/pull/2331 [FIX]
- https://github.com/qax-os/excelize/releases/tag/v2.11.0 [WEB]

### GO-2026-6453 — Unbounded memory allocation via streaming row reader in github.com/xuri/excelize
- Aliases: CVE-2026-59161, GHSA-q5j5-6p94-4gwc | Published: 2026-09-16 | Modified: 2026-09-17 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/github.com/xuri/excelize/v2: introduced:0 fixed:2.11.0

In github.com/xuri/excelize/v2, the streaming worksheet reader used by Rows and GetRows does not enforce the maximum row limit (TotalRows) on row "r" attributes. A crafted spreadsheet with an out-of-bounds row index causes GetRows to allocate empty row slices up to the specified row number, leading to excessive memory consumption and denial of service.

References:
- https://github.com/qax-os/excelize/security/advisories/GHSA-q5j5-6p94-4gwc [ADVISORY]
- https://github.com/qax-os/excelize/commit/93f0b3caed37f21ef5079e3259c6c21dcfe68453 [FIX]
- https://github.com/qax-os/excelize/pull/2331 [FIX]
- https://github.com/qax-os/excelize/releases/tag/v2.11.0 [WEB]

### GO-2026-6599 — Reset context tracking on consecutive template expressions in html/template
- Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-94448, CVE-2026-94448 | Published: 2026-10-08 | Modified: 2026-11-14 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.9 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.2

When a JavaScript template literal contains consecutive expressions, the context tracking state was not properly reset upon entering a new expression.

We now ensure that template-literal expression entries correctly reset context variables so all subsequent regular expression literals are accurately recognized and escaped.

A trusted template author may have previously written a valid template wherein the use of the 'yield' keyword would not be correctly escaped.

We now ensure that valid keyword uses are escaped and non-keyword uses are not escaped.

### GO-2026-6601 — Checksum bypass for golang.org/fips140 in cmd/go
- Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-94444, CVE-2026-94444 | Published: 2026-10-08 | Modified: 2026-11-14 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.9 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.2

Previously, a user operating inside of a malicious Go project that defines a bogus golang.org/fips140 and operates a malicious GOMODPROXY the user chooses to connect to can serve an arbitrary module in its place.

We now unpack the trusted ziphash for the bundled golang.org/fips140 module and construct its entry in the GOMODCACHE such that it can be verified by the toolchain.

- https://go.dev/cl/840685 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/81833 [REPORT]

### GO-2026-6602 — Checksum database bypass for golang.org/toolchain in cmd/go
- Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-94447, CVE-2026-94447 | Published: 2026-10-08 | Modified: 2026-11-14 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.9 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.2

Previously, a user operating inside of a malicious Go project that defines a bogus golang.org/toolchain go.sum entry and operates a malicious GOMODPROXY the user chooses to use can bypass the intended checksum.

We now ensure that golang.org/toolchain always goes to the network for the canonical checksum.

### GO-2026-6603 — HTTP/2 server memory exhaustion due to Trailer headers in net/http
- Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-78659, CVE-2026-78659 | Published: 2026-10-08 | Modified: 2026-11-14 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.9
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.2
- Affected Go/golang.org/x/net: introduced:0 fixed:0.60.0

When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP server internally uses the header values to populate the Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers, which do not support multiplexing a large number of requests over one TCP connection, and whose Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/847185 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/cl/847314 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/81857 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI [WEB]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/ZPwCyRUuGBs [WEB]

Credits: RyotaK (https://ryotak.net) of GMO Flatt Security Inc.

- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.9 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.2

On Windows, when the target of Root.Mkdir or Root.MkdirAll is a junction pointing to an empty location, the operation can create a directory at the junction target even when that target is located outside the root. This only applies to operations where the last path component is a junction (path/to/junction, but not path/junction/target).

### GO-2026-6605 — HTTP/1 client connection desynchronization after CONNECT rejection in net/http
- Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-56866, CVE-2026-56866 | Published: 2026-10-08 | Modified: 2026-11-14 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.9 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.2

When http.Transport sends an HTTP/1 CONNECT request with a non-empty Request.Body, it writes the body directly to the connection without framing after the request headers. If the server rejects the CONNECT request with a non-2xx keep-alive response, Transport returns the connection to the idle pool. Because CONNECT requests do not have a request body, the server may interpret the trailing body bytes as a subsequent pipelined HTTP/1.1 request on the connection, leaving the pooled connection desynchronized and causing the next caller that reuses it to read the response to the injected request. In reverse proxies (including httputil.ReverseProxy) that forward CONNECT requests through a shared Transport, this can lead to cross-user response poisoning.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/847306 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/81740 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI [WEB]

Credits: Xclow3n (Rajat Raghav)

### GO-2026-6607 — Reject malformed ECH outer extension references in crypto/tls
- Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-97031, CVE-2026-97031 | Published: 2026-10-08 | Modified: 2026-11-14 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.9 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.2

Multiple ECH outer extension references are not permitted under RFC 9849; previously, a client could send a well-crafted packet that could trigger memory exhaustion in the server process by specifying multiple references.

We now reject these as malformed and curb the memory amplification vector as a result.

### GO-2026-6610 — HTTP/2 transport accepts malformed framing-related headers in net/http
- Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-78660, CVE-2026-78660 | Published: 2026-10-08 | Modified: 2026-11-14 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.9
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.2
- Affected Go/golang.org/x/net: introduced:0 fixed:0.60.0

Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does not behave strictly enough, this can result in response smuggling.

### GO-2026-6612 — Double flow control refund on HTTP/2 server streams in net/http
- Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-78663, CVE-2026-78663 | Published: 2026-10-08 | Modified: 2026-11-14 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.9
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.2
- Affected Go/golang.org/x/net: introduced:0 fixed:0.60.0

The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the stream), and again when a request handler reads the buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is still limited by the concurrent stream limit and stream-level flow control.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/847187 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/cl/847310 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/81743 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI [WEB]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/ZPwCyRUuGBs [WEB]

Credits: Ali Sherif (https://www.linkedin.com/in/ali-sherif-13812b276/)

### GO-2026-6613 — HTTP/1 server connection desynchronization after 2xx CONNECT response in net/http
- Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-94439, CVE-2026-94439 | Published: 2026-10-08 | Modified: 2026-11-14 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.9 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.2

When an HTTP server handler sends a 2xx response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT request and returns without hijacking the connection, the server improperly continues to read and serve requests from the connection. Since a 2xx response to an HTTP/1 CONNECT converts the connection into a tunnel, the server should not treat the connection as continuing to contain HTTP.

The impact of this misbehavior is mostly limited to potential request smuggling, where an intermediate proxy considers the data on the connection to be tunneled and the server considers it to be HTTP.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/847311 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/81744 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI [WEB]

Credits: Jakub Ciolek (https://ciolek.dev)

### GO-2026-6617 — HTTP/2 server crash due to HPACK encoder race in net/http
- Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-97032, CVE-2026-97032 | Published: 2026-10-08 | Modified: 2026-11-14 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.9
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.2
- Affected Go/golang.org/x/net: introduced:0 fixed:0.60.0

HTTP/2 servers could end up crashing due to inadvertently modifying its HPACK encoder concurrently. This happens because the server modifies the HPACK encoder from two goroutines without synchronization: one uses the encoder to encode a HEADERS frame as part of a response sent to a client and the other modifies the encoder's table size when handling a SETTINGS frame containing SETTINGS_HEADER_TABLE_SIZE that a client sends. A malicious client can repeatedly send a request while changing the header table size to crash the server.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/847188 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/cl/847313 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/81867 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/U2fTuyDJznI [WEB]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/ZPwCyRUuGBs [WEB]

### GO-2026-6809 — Distrust compromised intermediate certificates in crypto/x509
- Aliases: BIT-golang-2026-111943, CVE-2026-111943, RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2026-0382, RUSTSEC-2026-0383 | Published: 2026-10-21 | Modified: 2026-11-14 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.10 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.3

On most platforms, Go uses the given system root certificates. However, in some narrower cases, the system trust stores may not be updated without further action.

To defend against the narrower set of cases that may remain affected, a denylist was added in crypto/x509 to return an error when calling Verify with any of the known intermediate certificates that are no longer considered to be trustworthy.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/851047 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82345 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/66pojueaQek [WEB]

### GO-2026-6860 — Avoid quadratic complexity when coalescing text nodes in html in golang.org/x/net
- Aliases: CVE-2026-78661 | Published: 2026-10-27 | Modified: 2026-10-27 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/golang.org/x/net: introduced:0 fixed:0.62.0

When coalescing adjacent text nodes in addText and fosterParent, appending to an existing TextNode's Data via string concatenation (n.Data += text) reallocated and copied the accumulated string on every token. Inputs containing many short text runs separated by ignored end tags (such as "a</x>") caused O(n^2) allocations and byte copies.

Accumulate coalesced text in per-node byte slices during parsing and materialize Data strings once at the end of parse.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/849365 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82224 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/sqrs2vTx_Xs [WEB]

Credits: Markus Magnuson

### GO-2026-6866 — Check all ancestor namespace transitions when rendering raw text in html in golang.org/x/net
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97045 | Published: 2026-10-27 | Modified: 2026-10-27 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/golang.org/x/net: introduced:0 fixed:0.62.0

In childTextNodesAreLiteral, walking up the tree previously stopped at the nearest foreign ancestor once an HTML integration point was found. However, that integration point may itself be a descendant of an element that was foster-parented into a foreign namespace (such as <mglyph> or <malignmark> fostered under <mtext>), causing a parser to resolve the subtree in a different foreign namespace upon re-parsing the rendered output.

Continue walking the full ancestor chain and verify that every transition from a non-empty namespace occurs at an HTML integration point before emitting literal text.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/855121 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82622 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/sqrs2vTx_Xs [WEB]

Credits: Ali Sherif (https://www.linkedin.com/in/ali-sherif-13812b276)

### GO-2026-6888 — Excessive memory allocation when decompressing crafted streams in github.com/andybalholm/brotli
- Aliases: BIT-brotli-2026-111497, BIT-dotnet-2026-111497, BIT-dotnet-sdk-2026-111497, BIT-node-2026-111497, BIT-node-min-2026-111497, BIT-powershell-2026-111497, CVE-2026-111497, GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35, GHSA-c9gr-gmg4-2vqv, PYSEC-2026-4322, PYSEC-2026-4323 | Published: 2026-11-05 | Modified: 2026-11-05 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/github.com/andybalholm/brotli: introduced:0 fixed:1.2.7

In github.com/andybalholm/brotli before v1.2.7, the decompressor allocates memory for Huffman tables and block-type trees on every meta-block header without bounding the cumulative allocations relative to the input size. A small crafted brotli stream containing many empty meta-blocks with new Huffman trees can trigger hundreds of megabytes of allocations per kilobyte of input, leading to denial of service.

### GO-2026-6893 — Event type spoofing via UntrustedType in github.com/google/go-eventlog
- Aliases:  | Published: 2026-11-05 | Modified: 2026-11-05 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/github.com/google/go-eventlog: introduced:0 fixed:0.0.3-0.20261001001437-1991f15bc4b0

In github.com/google/go-eventlog/tcg, Event exposes UntrustedType, which returns the raw event type header from the TCG event log without verifying that the event data matches its digest. Callers that dispatch on Event.UntrustedType after ParseAndReplay can be tricked by a modified event type field for events whose digests are not verified against EventData.

### GO-2026-6905 — Panic on negative member size in Reader.Read in github.com/blakesmith/ar
- Aliases:  | Published: 2026-11-05 | Modified: 2026-11-05 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/github.com/blakesmith/ar: introduced:0

Reader.Next parses the 10-byte decimal size field of an archive member header with strconv.ParseInt without rejecting negative values. A header with a negative size leaves the reader with a negative remaining byte count, causing the subsequent call to Reader.Read to panic with a slice bounds out of range error when slicing the caller's buffer.

### GO-2026-6909 — Nil-pointer panic in validateAssertion and namespace-blind Subject.NameID in github.com/crewjam/saml
- Aliases:  | Published: 2026-11-05 | Modified: 2026-11-05 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/github.com/crewjam/saml: introduced:0

github.com/crewjam/saml through v0.5.1 contains two vulnerabilities in SAML assertion processing:

1. ServiceProvider.validateAssertion dereferences assertion.Issuer without a nil check when ExpectedIDPEntityID is non-empty. A signed SAML assertion that omits the optional <saml:Issuer> element causes a nil-pointer dereference panic after signature verification.

2. Subject uses the bare XML struct tag xml:"NameID", which matches <NameID> elements in any XML namespace. When a signed assertion omits <saml:NameID> and includes a <NameID> element in a foreign namespace inside <saml:Subject>, encoding/xml populates Subject.NameID from the foreign element, allowing an authenticated principal to spoof Subject.NameID.Value.

### GO-2026-6911 — SSRF and credential leak via unvalidated Location header in github.com/mark3labs/mcp-go
- Aliases:  | Published: 2026-11-05 | Modified: 2026-11-05 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/github.com/mark3labs/mcp-go: introduced:0

In github.com/mark3labs/mcp-go/client/transport, NewStreamableHTTP constructs an http.Client with a nil CheckRedirect policy when no custom WithHTTPBasicClient is supplied, and attaches static custom headers and OAuth bearer tokens inside a RoundTripper layer. If an MCP server responds with a 3xx redirect, the client follows the Location header to arbitrary hosts and schemes and attaches configured WithHeaders and OAuth Authorization headers to the redirected request, enabling server-side request forgery (SSRF) and credential disclosure.

### GO-2026-6848 — Unexpected code execution via escaped quotes in //go:cgo_ldflag in cmd/go and cmd/compile
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97043 | Published: 2026-11-11 | Modified: 2026-11-11 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.11 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.4

Building a malicious package that uses cgo could bypass "#cgo LDFLAGS" validation and cause unexpected code execution at build time, or cause the go command to panic, via crafted quoting in "//go:cgo_ldflag" directives.

When "cmd/cgo" generates "_cgo_gotypes.go", it quotes each "#cgo LDFLAGS" argument with strconv.Quote in a "//go:cgo_ldflag" directive, but "cmd/compile" and "cmd/go" parsed those directives by splitting on raw quote characters without handling backslash escapes or unquoting the string. This mismatch allowed disallowed linker flags or unvalidated linker search paths to be smuggled past the go command's flag checks and passed to the external linker. In addition, deduplicating LDFLAGS in the go command could panic with an out-of-bounds slice index when a prefix of the flag list matched near the end of the slice.

"cmd/compile" and "cmd/go" now properly handle backslash-escaped quotes and unquote "//go:cgo_*" pragma strings with strconv.Unquote, and the slice bounds check in processCgoOutputs has been fixed.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/862156 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82567 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM [WEB]

### GO-2026-6849 — Linker flag injection via cgo_import_dynamic and PE DLL names in cmd/cgo, cmd/compile, and cmd/link
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97042 | Published: 2026-11-11 | Modified: 2026-11-11 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.11 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.4

Building a malicious package that uses "//go:cgo_import_dynamic" or links against a crafted PE object on Windows could pass unsafe library arguments to the external linker.

The compiler only checked the first character of the library name in "//go:cgo_import_dynamic" directives and skipped validation in cgo-generated files. In addition, on Windows, "cmd/cgo" and "cmd/link" did not validate imported DLL names extracted from PE object files before emitting "-l<name>" flags for the external linker, allowing a crafted DLL name containing ".." path traversal or special characters to reference arbitrary files on disk.

The compiler now validates every character of the library name in "//go:cgo_import_dynamic" directives (including in cgo-generated files on Windows) and rejects ".." path traversal, and "cmd/cgo" and "cmd/link" reject PE imported DLL names containing path separators, "..", ":", or leading "-" or "@".

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/862155 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82568 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM [WEB]

### GO-2026-6850 — Host linker flag injection via //go:cgo_* directives in cmd/compile and cmd/link
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97041 | Published: 2026-11-11 | Modified: 2026-11-11 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.11 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.4

Building a malicious package containing "//go:cgo_*" compiler directives could inject arbitrary flags into the external linker invocation on ELF platforms.

The compiler and linker did not reject commas in "//go:cgo_import_dynamic", "//go:cgo_export_dynamic", "//go:cgo_export_static", "//go:cgo_import_static", and "//go:cgo_dynamic_linker" directives, and the linker passed the dynamic linker path using "-Wl,--dynamic-linker,<path>". Furthermore, the two-argument form of "//go:cgo_import_dynamic" (which is permitted in non-cgo Go source files) could overwrite the external symbol name of a symbol already marked for cgo export. A symbol name or dynamic linker path containing a comma or leading "@" could split "-Wl,--export-dynamic-symbol=" or "-Wl,--dynamic-linker," into arbitrary host linker flags or response file arguments.

The compiler and linker now reject commas in "//go:cgo_*" symbol and dynamic linker directives, the linker passes "-Wl,--dynamic-linker=<path>", and "cgo_import_dynamic" no longer overwrites symbols exported via "cgo_export_dynamic" or "cgo_export_static".

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/862154 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82569 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM [WEB]

### GO-2026-6851 — Cgo directive injection via .syso files disguised as Go object files in cmd/go and cmd/link
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97040 | Published: 2026-11-11 | Modified: 2026-11-11 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.11 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.4

Building a package containing a crafted ".syso" file could bypass cgo flag validation and inject arbitrary linker flags when linking.

When loading ".syso" entries from a package archive, the linker only checked for recognized host object headers (ELF, Mach-O, PE, and XCOFF) before falling through to Go object parsing. A ".syso" file beginning with a "go object" header was parsed as a Go compiler object, allowing untrusted cgo metadata directives (such as "cgo_ldflag" or "cgo_dynamic_linker") embedded in the ".syso" file to be passed to the external linker without validation. Additionally, ".syso" filenames longer than 16 bytes lost their ".syso" extension when truncated in archive headers, and unrecognized ".syso" formats forced external linking in pure-Go builds.

The linker now rejects ".syso" files that are not recognized host object formats, and "cmd/go" and "cmd/pack" preserve the ".syso" suffix when truncating long archive member names.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/862153 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82570 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM [WEB]

Credits: RyotaK (https://ryotak.net) of GMO Flatt Security Inc.

### GO-2026-6852 — Flag sanitization bypass via "#cgo pkg-config:" directives in cmd/go
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97039 | Published: 2026-11-11 | Modified: 2026-11-11 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.11 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.4

Building a malicious package that uses "#cgo pkg-config:" directives could load untrusted pkg-config ".pc" files or inject unvalidated compiler and linker flags.

The pkg-config flag allowlist previously permitted "--with-path=" and "--personality=", allowed "--define-variable=" values beginning with "=" or "$" (which can rewrite paths in system ".pc" files into sysroot-prefixed "-L=" or "-L$SYSROOT" linker search paths), and allowed package arguments ending in ".pc" or containing path separators or "..", which caused pkg-config to load local ".pc" files directly from the package directory. In addition, flags returned by "pkg-config --cflags" in cgoCPPFLAGS were not checked when determining whether internal linking is safe.

The go command now disallows "--with-path=", "--personality=", leading "=" or "$" characters in "--define-variable=" values, and local ".pc" paths in "#cgo pkg-config:" directives, and inspects cgoCPPFLAGS when checking internal linking compatibility.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/862152 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82571 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM [WEB]

### GO-2026-6853 — Arbitrary code execution via crafted .syso files and cgo linker input files in cmd/go
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97038 | Published: 2026-11-11 | Modified: 2026-11-11 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.11 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.4

Building a malicious package containing ".syso" files or cgo linker inputs could inject arbitrary linker flags or execute arbitrary code at link time.

Linker input files—including ".syso" files, direct object or library inputs in "#cgo LDFLAGS", and libraries in "-L" directories—were passed to the external linker without validating their format or checking for embedded linker options. Across platforms, this allowed executing GNU ld implicit linker scripts disguised as libraries or ".syso" files (or loaded via "-l:<filename>" or "-l" containing path separators), injecting unallowlisted linker flags via PE/COFF ".drectve" sections on Windows or Mach-O "LC_LINKER_OPTION" load commands on Darwin, or invoking LTO plugins via GCC or LLVM LTO intermediate representation sections in ELF, PE/COFF, or Mach-O objects.

The go command now verifies that ".syso" files, direct linker inputs, and libraries in "-L" directories are valid binary objects or archives that do not contain unallowlisted ".drectve" directives, "LC_LINKER_OPTION" load commands, or LTO IR sections, and disallows "-l:<filename>" and ":", "=", or path separators in "-l" flags.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/862151 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82572 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM [WEB]

### GO-2026-6854 — Linker script injection via split -Wl, flags and Darwin or symbol linker flags in cgo in cmd/go
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97037 | Published: 2026-11-11 | Modified: 2026-11-11 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.11 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.4

Building a malicious package that uses cgo could cause arbitrary code execution at link time by passing linker script files to the host linker via "#cgo LDFLAGS".

Split "-Wl," flags that consume a following argument (such as "-Wl,-rpath", "-Wl,--just-symbols", and "-Wl,-undefined") previously accepted a bare second argument without a "-Wl," prefix, which the compiler driver passes directly to the linker as a positional input file. Additionally, when using GNU ld.bfd, flags such as "-framework", "-Wl,-framework", "-Wl,-undefined", "-Wl,--just-symbols", "-Wl,-R", "-Wl,-subsystem", and (on non-Darwin platforms) "-Wl,-sectcreate" could cause ld.bfd to interpret their arguments as linker scripts if they named a regular file on disk.

The go command now requires a "-Wl," prefix on the second token of split "-Wl," flags (except "-Wl,-R"), verifies that these flags do not reference linker script files, and disallows bare "-Wl,--warn-backrefs-exclude".

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/862150 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82573 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM [WEB]

### GO-2026-6855 — Arbitrary code execution during build on darwin via "-l to_library" in cgo in cmd/go
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97036 | Published: 2026-11-11 | Modified: 2026-11-11 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.11 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.4

On Darwin, building a malicious package that uses cgo could cause arbitrary code execution when using the Apple linker due to passing "-l to_library <path>" in a "#cgo LDFLAGS" directive.

The Apple linker recombines the separated arguments "-l" and "to_library" into "-lto_library", which loads an arbitrary LTO plugin dynamic library at link time.

The go command now disallows "-l" followed by "to_library" in "#cgo LDFLAGS", rejects "-lazy_library", "-lazy_framework", "-load_hidden", "-library", and "-library-path", and checks recombined "-l" arguments against disallowed linker flags and patterns.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/862149 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82574 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM [WEB]

Credits: Ali Sherif (https://www.linkedin.com/in/ali-sherif-13812b276/)

### GO-2026-6856 — Unexpected code execution and arbitrary file write via Clang -gen-* and GCC -gnat* flags in cgo in cmd/go
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97035 | Published: 2026-11-11 | Modified: 2026-11-11 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.11 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.4

When using Clang or GCC, building a malicious package that uses cgo could cause unexpected code execution at build time or write files to arbitrary directories via "-gen-*" or "-gnat*" flags in "#cgo" directives.

The "-g*" wildcard in the compiler and linker flag allowlists previously matched Clang's two-argument "-gen-cdb-fragment-path <dir>" flag and GCC's two-argument "-gnatO <file>" flag, permitting compilation database fragments and sidecar output files to be written to arbitrary directories and desynchronizing flag argument parsing between the go command and the compiler driver so that subsequent arguments could be passed as unvalidated positional inputs to the linker.

"-gen-*" and "-gnat*" flags are now disallowed in "#cgo" compiler and linker flags.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/862148 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82575 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM [WEB]

### GO-2026-6857 — Arbitrary command execution via GCC spec files in cgo linker search directories in cmd/go
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97034 | Published: 2026-11-11 | Modified: 2026-11-11 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.11 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.4

When using GCC, building a malicious package that uses cgo could cause arbitrary command execution at link time via untrusted GCC spec files ("specs" or "*.spec").

When linking with "-fopenmp", "-fopenacc", or "-fsanitize=" in "#cgo LDFLAGS", GCC's built-in link spec evaluates "%:include(libgomp.spec)" or "%:include(libsanitizer.spec)" and searches for spec files in "-L" and sysroot directories (including subdirectories and multilib sibling directories such as "../lib64"), as well as the working directory when "-fopenmp" or "-fopenacc" is used or when "-fsanitize=" is combined with "-static" or "-static-lib*".

The go command now rejects "-L", "-isysroot", and "-Wl,-syslibroot" directories (and the working and package directories when applicable) that contain GCC spec files, and disallows "@" and "-" prefixes in "-fsanitize=" compiler flag values.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/862147 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82576 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM [WEB]

### GO-2026-6858 — Unexpected code execution via --sysroot, -target, -isysroot, -Wl,-syslibroot, and -x cgo flags in cmd/go
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97033 | Published: 2026-11-11 | Modified: 2026-11-11 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/toolchain: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.11 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.4

Building a malicious package that uses cgo could cause arbitrary code execution at build time through several compiler and linker flags permitted in "#cgo" directives.

Specifically, "--sysroot" in GCC and Clang relocates compiler subprograms, spec files, and CRT startup objects to an attacker-controlled directory; "-target" in Clang falls back to executing target helper tools from the current working directory when not found in PATH; "-isysroot" and "-Wl,-syslibroot" can pass a regular file on disk to GNU ld.bfd, which interprets it as a positional linker script; and "-x" permitted specifying arbitrary compiler input languages beyond those supported by cgo.

"--sysroot" and "-target" are now disallowed in "#cgo" flags, "-isysroot" and "-Wl,-syslibroot" are verified not to point to regular files, and "-x" is restricted to the C, C++, Objective-C, and assembler languages supported by cgo.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/862146 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82577 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM [WEB]

### GO-2026-6859 — HTTP/1 server crash due to MaxBytesReader header race in net/http
- Aliases: CVE-2026-97054 | Published: 2026-11-11 | Modified: 2026-11-11 | Severity: None
- Affected Go/stdlib: introduced:0 fixed:1.26.11 introduced:1.27.0-0 fixed:1.27.4

For HTTP/1 servers, when MaxBytesReader's limit is exceeded, "Connection: close" header is automatically set without synchronization, which might race with another header being set explicitly in the server handler. As a result, an HTTP/1 server that utilizes MaxBytesReader or MaxBytesHandler can crash due to runtime panic if its handler reads the request body concurrently with writing the response header.

References:
- https://go.dev/cl/862185 [FIX]
- https://go.dev/issue/82563 [REPORT]
- https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/iY8TY0wWgbM [WEB]
